solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Criticise one Conservative leader acting out of fear?

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly, as a reviewer does
I is the Roman numeral one
a king is a leader of a nation

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a Tory chief who seems to be behaving from fright.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone panicking is behaving under the grip of sudden alarm, so the verb form matches the phrase.

clue.text: Model soldier beginning to get on

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: beginning to says take only the first letter of get

explanation.surface: An exemplary soldier starting to make progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A paragon is a perfect example to follow, a model of excellence.

clue.text: Wise man in comfy position getting nothing right

parts.note: a nest is a snug, comfortable place
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sage sits snugly in a cosy spot, getting nothing correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestor was the elderly counsellor of the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.
explanation.definitionFit: Nestor's name is used for any wise old adviser, after the Homeric elder.

clue.text: Artist shows bird crossing river

indicators.note: crossing says the bird spans the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a coot is a water bird

explanation.surface: A painter exhibits a bird flying over a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a French landscape painter of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Female lacking in passion and anger

indicators.note: lacking in says the female letter is missing from the passion word

parts.note: fire means passion, ardour

explanation.surface: A woman without ardour, yet full of fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary synonym for wrath or rage.

clue.text: Accepted things from dealer and was sacked

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally received a hand at cards
second meaning: the British idiom for being dismissed from a job, when one's employment cards were handed back

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain an employee's National Insurance cards were returned on dismissal, hence the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes receiving a dealt hand and idiomatically means being fired from work.

clue.text: Country knocked back in great lamentations

indicators.note: knocked back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the country sits inside the words great lamentations

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A nation is devastated by grief and wailing.
explanation.walkthrough: ATLAM sits inside greAT LAMentations; 'in' signals the hiding and 'knocked back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is an island nation in the Mediterranean, a straightforward example of a country.

clue.text: Fit for the match

parts.note: sounds like a sports player ready to play, but the match is a wedding

explanation.walkthrough: Match suggests a game and fit suggests athletic fitness; the match is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone suitable for wedlock, especially by age or status, is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Member joining top celebrities: one sticking to the law

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
the A-list is the group of the most famous stars

explanation.surface: Someone joining the elite of the famous turns out to be a stickler for rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A legalist adheres strictly to the letter of law or rules.

clue.text: After short break, pressing to be on the up again

indicators.note: short says the word for break loses its final letter

parts.note: a rest is a break
pressing means urgent

explanation.surface: After a brief pause, someone is keen to climb once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something rising again after a decline, such as a revived team or economy.

clue.text: Type of music when Georgia goes to student event?

indicators.note: goes to says the Georgia letters are attached after the event

parts.note: a rag is a British student charity event, often a week of stunts
GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: Asks what kind of music gets played when a girl called Georgia attends a student party.
explanation.walkthrough: Georgia looks like a girl's name but supplies the state abbreviation GA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragga is a style of Jamaican dance music derived from reggae and dancehall.

clue.text: Spirited community?

parts.note: spirited usually means lively, but here it means full of spirits, i.e. phantoms

explanation.walkthrough: A lively town is the picture; the place is in fact deserted, haunted only by spectres.
explanation.definitionFit: An abandoned settlement is jokingly peopled only by phantoms, which is the pun on spirited.

clue.text: In charge of you and me. editor may be worn out

parts.note: over means in charge of, as in authority over
us means you and me

explanation.surface: A boss over the two of us, the editor may be exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: Overused means used so much it has become tired or stale, like a hackneyed phrase.

clue.text: Strangers in a story by Poles

parts.note: a story can be a lie, a fib
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Foreigners feature in a tale told by Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland but gives the two compass poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Aliens are foreigners or outsiders, people unfamiliar to a place.

clue.text: Jumps around plants

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as a verb, skips and frolics about
second meaning: caper shrubs, whose buds are pickled

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests someone leaping round a flowerbed; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both playful leaps and the Mediterranean shrubs whose flower buds are eaten pickled.

clue.text: Bill with long hair is a performer

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone named Bill with flowing locks is an entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name, but it is an invoice, an account.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a female performer on stage or screen.

clue.text: Northbound David in an American state

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed
in puts the David name inside the letters of an

parts.note: Dave is short for David

explanation.surface: A man called David travels north through a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Nevada is one of the fifty United States, home of Las Vegas.

clue.text: Former abstainer, party-goer at heart who is outward-looking?

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: at heart puts the party-goer in the middle of the abstainer letters

parts.note: TT means teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol
a raver is someone who goes to wild parties

explanation.surface: Describes an ex-teetotaller who is really a party animal and who looks outwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An extravert, a variant spelling of extrovert, is a sociable person whose interest is directed outside the self.

clue.text: A second group offering something worth having

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A further band presents something valuable.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful or valuable thing or quality.

clue.text: One getting up only a bit of the stairs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who rises from bed

definitions.text: only a bit of the stairs
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the vertical part of a single step in a staircase

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone climbing just a little way; the two phrases are two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a person who gets out of bed and the upright board between treads on steps.

clue.text: Football player, male with little energy and out of view

parts.note: a back is a defensive player in football
a stag is a male deer
E is the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: A footballer, a man low on energy, is out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage means behind the scenes, hidden from the audience.

clue.text: Odd characters in Corby yell

indicators.note: odd characters means the first, third and fifth letters of the town name

explanation.surface: Strange people in an English town shout.
explanation.walkthrough: Corby is a town in Northamptonshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry can mean to shout out loudly, a synonym of yell.

clue.text: Teams start to struggle before day in Rome

indicators.note: before puts the first letter ahead of the day
start to says take only the opening letter of struggle

parts.note: the Ides was a day of the month in the ancient Roman calendar

explanation.surface: Teams begin to falter just before a match day in the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Roman calendar the Ides fell on the 13th or 15th of the month.
explanation.definitionFit: Sides are teams in a game, as in picking sides.

clue.text: More than one African agent I spy being "shifty"

indicators.note: shifty, in quotes, says the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A secret agent from Africa is acting suspiciously.
explanation.definitionFit: Egyptians are people from Egypt, a country in Africa, and the plural matches 'more than one'.
